title: Alexander the Great

cards.h: He conquered the world by 32 and then his army said no more
cards.b:
Alexander of Macedon became king at 20 and died at 32. In between, he marched about 20,000 km, defeated the mighty Persian Empire and reached the edge of India.

Why did he stop? And how did he die? Read on.

Alexander was born in 356 BCE in Pella, Macedon. His father, Philip II, had built a mighty army. His tutor was the philosopher Aristotle. He tamed the wild horse Bucephalus as a boy.

In 336 BCE Philip was assassinated and Alexander became king.
Alexander's army was small but skilled and he led from the front. At Gaugamela (331 BCE) he beat a much larger Persian force. He took Babylon and Susa, and burned Persepolis in 330 BCE.

cards.h: To the end of the known world
cards.b:
He marched through Afghanistan and Central Asia, and into the Punjab. In 326 BCE, at the river Hydaspes (Jhelum), he defeated King Porus. Greek writers say he was so impressed that he gave Porus's land back.

Then, at the river Hyphasis (Beas), his weary soldiers refused to go on. After years of fighting, they wanted to go home.

Alexander died on about 10-11 June 323 BCE, in Babylon, aged 32, after a fever of about ten days. Causes debated: typhoid, malaria, alcohol, poison. Many theories, no proof.

Asked who should inherit, he supposedly said, 'to the strongest'. Historians doubt it. His generals, the Diadochi, split the empire. Ptolemy took Egypt, Seleucus most of Asia.

Alexander founded many cities named Alexandria. The one in Egypt became a centre of learning. Greek language and culture spread across Asia, giving the 'Hellenistic' world.

He also left chaos, destruction and thousands dead. Admirers and critics have fought about him for 2,000 years.

Myth: Alexander conquered India.Fact: he reached the Punjab, the north-west edge, and spent about two years there. He turned back. No Indian source records him by name. Greek writers are our main evidence.

It is true he never lost a major battle, but Hydaspes was costly, and his men were exhausted.

The vacuum that Chandragupta filled

Alexander crossed the Indus in 326 BCE and beat Porus at the Hydaspes (Jhelum). At the Beas his tired army refused to march on. By 325 he had turned back down the Indus.

In Magadha the Nanda king Dhana Nanda was hated and heavily taxed. Greek writers say he had 200,000 foot-soldiers and 6,000 elephants. Alexander's retreat left the Punjab with no master.

A young exile, Chandragupta Maurya, with the adviser Chanakya, toppled the Nandas around 321 BCE and took the north-west from the Greek governors. In 305 BCE he faced Seleucus Nicator, who ceded territory for 500 elephants. Megasthenes then came as ambassador to Pataliputra.

Five things to remember

  1. Alexander ruled Macedon from 336 and died in 323 BCE.
  2. He beat Persia at Issus and Gaugamela.
  3. At the Hydaspes (326 BCE) he beat Porus.
  4. His death is unexplained.
  5. The Mauryas rose soon after.

Think about it

  • Is 'the Great' the right title for him?
  • Why might Indian sources not mention him?
